newsitem.title: USA: Hayes to offer limited number of x2 modems.
newsitem.headline: Hayes to offer limited number of x2 modems.

text.p: Hayes Microcomputer Products Inc said Thursday it shipped a limited number of high-speed modems using U.S. Robotics Corp's x2 technology but remains commited to a rival alliance of modem makers.

"Because USR server customers are locked into buying the x2 technology or client modems, in order to provide an option for these customers, we are offering a very limited number of Practical Peripherals-branded products using the x2 technology," Kerri Dimke, spokeswoman for Atlanta, Ga.-based Hayes, said in a telephone interview.
"We're not changing our stance," Dimke said.

However, Hayes, which is second in U.S. modem market share, continues to support the K56Flex technology as the possible standard. The K56Flex is used by an alliance, including U.S. Robotics' rivals Rockwell International Corp, Motorola Inc and Lucent Technologies Inc.
Dimke said all Hayes-branded modems and most Practical Peripherals-branded modems will use K56Flex technology. She said those products will be shipped in the last week of March.
"We don't expect x2 to be the standard. We expect K56flex or something close to it to be the standard," Dimke said.
The 56-kilobit-per-second standard is still under debate. To get the high-speed connection, both the consumer modem and the service provider's hub must use the same technology.
Dimke said the Hayes-manufactured modems using the x2 technology will likely be on retail shelves on Sunday, but Hayes is only shipping them to a limited number of stores.
"We are meeting the initial customer demand because we feel it's not responsible to our customers...to say 'Sorry, we're not going to support that'," Dimke said. "It just makes good business sense."
Dimke said it is also part of the company's plan to grab consumer modem market share from U.S. Robotics, the top seller.
